subject: RAG qualification sprint — recommended models, evals & next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Hoffman <lena@aurumlabs.com>, Arjun Kumar <akumar@aurumlabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: RAG qualification sprint — kickoff recap and suggested next steps

Hi Lena / Arjun —

Thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep the momentum going on the RAG qualification:

What we heard you care about
- High-quality grounding (low hallucination) for regulatory Q&A and internal SOPs
- End-to-end P95 latency target <= 500ms for single-turn Q&A in production
- Predictable unit costs for token-level billing and caching opportunities

Initial model & retrieval recommendations (shortlist for the sprint)
- Candidate base models (for generation):
  - Llama2-13B-chat (quantized) — strong instruction-following baseline, lower cost
  - Mistral-7B-instruct — good tradeoff for factual precision on short answers
  - Redwood-verified Llama2-70B-chat (quantized) — if you need higher factuality and can accept higher cost
- Embedding/retrieval: dense embeddings via sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 for initial sprint; consider hybrid (sparse+dense) if recall drops on long policy docs
- Reranker: cascade design (bi-encoder candidate retrieval -> cross-encoder rerank). Cross-encoder candidate: ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-cross for initial runs.

Suggested retrieval settings to start (we will tune):
- chunk size 700–900 tokens, 128 token overlap
- vector index: HNSW (efConstruction 200), efSearch 128; nprobe-like equivalent = 32
- recall targets: recall@20 >= 0.85 on your sample queries

Evals & benchmarks we propose during the 2-week sprint
- Grounding metrics: grounding_rate (fraction of answers with at least one citation that matches indexed doc), hallucination_rate (manual adjudication on sample set), reranker_precision@5, recall@20, exact_match for extractive QA where applicable
- Latency: cold vs warm KV-cache p50/p95 on end-to-end pipeline
- Cost: token and compute estimates per 1K queries at expected QPS

Action items (what we need from you)
1) Provide a 300–500 query seed set (representative Qs) + golden citations if available (we'll use for grounding checks).
2) Sandbox access: either API key or short-term S3 access to the doc corpus + a sample export.
3) Confirm P95 latency target and any hard SLAs for availability / retention.

I've attached: aurum_rag_benchmark_v1.csv (example benchmark schema) and prompt_suite_seed_v2.txt (starter prompts). I'll spin up the sprint repo and share links once you confirm items 1–3.

Thanks — planning to schedule the first technical sync next Tue. If that works for you, ping preferred times.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference

Karthik —

Thanks for the clear plan. A few clarifying Qs before we hand over the corpus:
1) Reranker latency: our internal SLA target for user-facing Q&A is p95 <= 500ms — does the cross-encoder approach you suggested fit that budget end-to-end?
2) For the seed set: we can deliver ~400 queries by EOD Monday. Some of those are multi-part and cite multiple docs — is that OK?
3) Security: can we get a short description of your data handling for private doc uploads (retention, encryption at rest, who can access the corpus)?

Also cc’ing our procurement lead (sales@aurumlabs.com) — procurement will want the mutual action plan and a rough cost estimate for a small pilot (10k queries / month).

Lena
Head of Product, Aurum Labs
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Hoffman <lena@aurumlabs.com>, Arjun Kumar <akumar@aurumlabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 26 Mar 2027 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RAG qualification sprint — kickoff recap and suggested next steps

Lena — thanks, quick answers + more detail so procurement/eng have what they need. (Quoting your questions inline.)

> 1) Reranker latency: our internal SLA target for user-facing Q&A is p95 <= 500ms — does the cross-encoder approach you suggested fit that budget end-to-end?

Short answer: yes for pilot-scale traffic if we adopt a cascade (bi-encoder candidate retrieval -> small cross-encoder on top of top-K=50 candidates) and apply these controls:
- Keep cross-encoder small (MiniLM-style) for rerank step; expect ~60–120ms per query on a single CPU-optimized instance for the rerank stage with batch size 8.
- Use shard-local reranking and warm KV cache for generated contexts to hit p95 <= 500ms for single-turn.
- If p95 tightens under load, fallback policy: run bi-encoder-only at high QPS and enable asynchronous cross-encoder re-rank for background quality tracking.

Estimated perf numbers (pilot):
- Retrieval (dense) + top-50 candidates: ~40–80ms
- Cross-encoder rerank (MiniLM): ~70–120ms
- Generator model (Llama2-13B q4): p50 ~120ms, p95 ~260–480ms depending on token length and quantization.
- End-to-end p95 estimate: 340–520ms (depends on prompt length & token generation; we'll run controlled microbenchmarks).

> 2) For the seed set: we can deliver ~400 queries by EOD Monday. Some of those are multi-part and cite multiple docs — is that OK?

Yes — multi-part queries actually help exercise grounding. Please mark golden citations where available; we'll use those in the grounding_rate computation.

> 3) Security: can we get a short description of your data handling for private doc uploads (retention, encryption at rest, who can access the corpus)?

Short summary for procurement:
- Data at rest encrypted with customer-managed KMS (optionally) or Redwood-managed keys.
- Access to ingested corpus restricted to the sprint environment and explicitly listed engineers; logs and audit trail retained per the mutual action plan.
- We can supply a one-page security summary and a SOC2 checklist for your security review (I will loop Security if you want the full package).

Proposed evaluation metrics and experiment plan (high level)
- Metrics: grounding_rate, hallucination_rate (manual adjudication on a 200-sample gold set), recall@20, reranker_precision@5, end-to-end p95 latency, PCR (prompt-context relevance score) as internal heuristic.
- Experiments:
  1) Retriever comparison: dense-only vs sparse+dense hybrid. Track recall@20 & latency.
  2) Reranker ablation: bi-encoder-only vs cascade (bi -> small cross-encoder) vs full cross-encoder. Track reranker_precision@5 and added latency.
  3) Generator model fit: run same prompt suite across Llama2-13B, Mistral-7B, Redwood-verified Llama2-70B. Compare grounding_rate and hallucination_rate.

I've uploaded a starter benchmark sheet to the shared drive and attached aurum_rag_benchmark_v1.csv and prompt_suite_seed_v2.txt. Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AurumShared/benchmark-sheets and our internal eval run: https://redwood-internal.example.com/evals/aurum-rag-2027

Next steps I propose:
- You share the seed queries + sample corpus by Mon 29 Mar.
- We run an initial retrieval + reranker sweep and return a short readout w/ perf and grounding metrics within 5 business days.
- Schedule tech sync Tues 30 Mar — please share 30/60/90 min slots.

I'll also prepare a short mutual action plan doc for procurement.

—Karthik
